name: Joseph
bio: A young man in Paris, described by Wilde in December 1898 as I. D. W. Ashton's 'little friend'. He lived in the same establishment as Ashton and served at table when sober. Wilde's letter has him returning with a black eye and a swollen nose after drink and a political discussion, then vanishing from a Sunday morning until the next day; Wilde calls him 'a little Dionysiac' and blames Ashton's habit of giving good advice for driving him to drink. No surname, age, occupation beyond waiting at table, or later trace appears in the pages read.
bio_note: Sole source: Wilde to Reginald Turner, [postmark 6 December 1898], Hotel d'Alsace, Paris, Complete Letters (2000), p. 1107.
